attribution.note: The parenthetical is Marcus's own comment, added to his description of Tao's distinction. He wrote it and endorsed it in his own newsletter.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the hedge on the open-problem clause ('seems', 'perhaps with some important limits') and keeps 'thus far'. The firm, checkable part is the observation that there was no evidence of theory-building up to the post date.

contract.note: Marcus gave no definition of 'building theory'. The plain reading (developing concepts, definitions or frameworks beyond a single solution) is ordinary and fair. Treating the hedged open-problem clause as unscored is correct. The result depends on how theory-building is judged.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own Aug 1 announcement credits ten results to Astra. It is a company disclosure and does not address theory-building either way.

Tao's slides, dated before the post, separate theory-building from problem-solving but do not assess Astra. The packet labels them a company disclosure, which is wrong, but the item is real and relevant as context.

The original Aug 1 manuscript describes a new structural ingredient in one proof. It could be a counterexample, but nothing in the packet assesses whether it amounts to theory-building, so it does not settle the claim.

reviews.rationale: The firm part of the claim is that there was no evidence of Astra building theory by Aug 3, 2026. The packet has no comprehensive expert assessment showing such evidence was absent. The original manuscript (e3) contains new constructions, but nobody in the packet establishes that they count as theory-building. Neither the support condition nor the contradiction condition is met, and failing to find evidence in a search does not prove the evidence was absent.
